description: Constraint layer. Creative rules and extra challenges are what turn a random draw into a real brief. Difficulty: 1 = easy, 2 = medium, 3 = hard. Tags exist so future filters/collections can slice the pool without touching generator code.

difficulties.name: Easy
difficulties.note: One constraint. Move fast, keep it fun.

difficulties.name: Medium
difficulties.note: Two constraints that fight each other a little.

difficulties.name: Hard
difficulties.note: Constraints that remove something you rely on.

difficulties.name: Insane
difficulties.note: You will want to quit. Finish it anyway.

arrangements.name: Short Loop
arrangements.note: 8 to 16 bars. No structure, just the idea.

arrangements.name: Two-Part Switch
arrangements.note: Change the beat completely halfway through.

arrangements.name: Intro + Outro Only
arrangements.note: Write the bookends. Leave the middle empty.

arrangements.name: Interlude
arrangements.note: Under 90 seconds. It should feel unfinished on purpose.

arrangements.name: Triple Switch
arrangements.note: Three distinct sections, one continuous track.

arrangements.name: One-Take Jam
arrangements.note: Perform the arrangement live in one pass.

arrangements.name: Skit Intro
arrangements.note: Open with dialogue or found audio before the beat drops.

arrangements.name: Loop Pack
arrangements.note: Three variations of the same 4 bars.

arrangements.name: Verse Only
arrangements.note: One 16-bar section that repeats. No hook.

arrangements.name: Ambient Intro
arrangements.note: 30 seconds of texture before any drums.

chordStyles.name: Two-Note Voicings
chordStyles.note: Root and one interval. That's the whole harmony.

chordStyles.name: Diminished Tension
chordStyles.note: Use it as a passing chord, not a home.

chordStyles.name: Modal Vamp
chordStyles.note: Two chords for the whole track. Live in the mode.

chordStyles.name: Single Chord Drone
chordStyles.note: One chord. The movement comes from texture.

chordStyles.name: Chromatic Movement
chordStyles.note: Slide the same shape by semitones.

creativeRules.text: Use only one sample for the entire beat.
No kick drum anywhere in the track.
No snare. Find another way to mark the backbeat.
Mix the entire beat in mono.
Reverse the intro.
No EQ on any channel.
Finish the beat in 30 minutes.
Turn quantization off completely.
No piano of any kind.
No bass line. Let the sample carry the low end.
Use only stock plugins.
One melodic instrument for the whole beat.
Major chords only.
Minor chords only.
Everything must be sampled. No synths at all.
No hi-hats for the first 16 bars.
Vinyl crackle must be audible from start to finish.
Maximum 8 tracks.
Audio clips only. No MIDI instruments.
Pitch every sample down at least 3 semitones.
Include at least one vocal chop.
Never repeat the same 4 bars twice identically.
No compressor on the master bus.
The drums must be louder than everything else.
Build the entire kit from one drum break.
No reverb anywhere.
Reverb on every single channel.
Only use sounds you recorded yourself today.
The beat must change key at least once.
Start with the outro and work backwards.
No open hi-hats.
The kick must be distorted.
Use exactly three sounds. No more.
Every element must be sidechained to the kick.
Write the bass line before anything else.
No looping. Every bar must be placed by hand.
Include a full bar of silence somewhere.
Nothing above 10kHz. Low-pass the master.
Use only one plugin per channel.
The melody must be played with one finger.
No presets. Design every synth patch from init.
The whole beat must sit under 90 seconds.
Sample something recorded before 1970.
Sample something recorded after 2020.
Reverse one sample and leave it reversed.
Use a sample in a language you don't speak.
Only percussion. No pitched instruments at all.
No drums until the halfway point.
Chop the sample into 16 slices and reorder them randomly.
The hook must be a sound, not a melody.
Use only white noise for the hi-hats.
Never use the same drum hit twice at the same velocity.
The snare must be off-grid by at least 20ms.
Everything must be recorded in one take.
No copy and paste. At all.
Only two chords for the entire beat.
Use a time signature that isn't 4/4.
The beat must start on the 'and' of 1.
Add a tape stop somewhere.
One instrument must be completely out of tune.
Bounce the beat, reimport it, and process the bounce.
No plugin may exceed 30% wet.
Sample a sound from your kitchen.
Only use sounds under 1 second long.
The intro must last at least 30 seconds.
No cymbals of any kind.
Use only one octave for every melodic part.
Layer three snares tuned to the same note.
Make the hi-hats the loudest element.
The beat must fade in from silence over 8 bars.
No fade outs. It has to end on a hit.
Use a sample with no drums in it.
Use a sample that already has drums and keep them.
Pitch the sample up until it sounds wrong, then keep it.
Use only mono samples.
Delete your favourite element before you finish.
Every sound must be panned hard left or hard right.
Nothing may be panned. Everything dead centre.
The drums must be quieter than the sample.
Write the melody by humming it first.
Do not use headphones. Speakers only.
Do not look at the waveform. Mix by ear only.
Do not use a metronome.
No velocity editing. Whatever you played, stays.
Every drum hit must be triggered from a pad or key, never drawn.
Use a field recording as the hi-hat.
Add crowd noise or room tone under the whole beat.
One element must play backwards the whole time.
Use a 12-bit or lower bit depth on everything.
No stereo widening tools.
The bass must never play the root note.
The melody must use exactly five notes.
No note may last longer than an eighth note.
Every chord must be held for at least 2 bars.
Use a drone under the entire track.
Change the tempo at least once mid-track.
Automate the filter cutoff across the whole song.
No automation whatsoever.
Build the beat starting from the hi-hats.
Build the beat starting from the ad-libs or textures.
The first sound the listener hears must be non-musical.
End the beat on an unresolved chord.
Use only sounds that start with the letter of your first name.
Name the beat before you make it, then make it fit the name.
Do not open any folder you have used in the last month.
Use the first sample you find. No skipping.
Only use samples from a genre you dislike.
Sample a song released in the year you were born.
Every sound must pass through the same reverb bus.
Use a delay with feedback above 70% somewhere.
No snare rolls, no hat rolls, no fills.
Every 8 bars something must be removed, never added.
Use a sound from a video game.
Include a sample of someone speaking.
No claps.
Replace the snare with a non-drum sound.
Replace the kick with a non-drum sound.
Use a chord that doesn't belong to the key.
Everything must be in the same key as the sample. No pitching.
Only use black keys on the keyboard.
Only use white keys on the keyboard.
Record the melody with a microphone, not MIDI.
The beat must work with the drums muted.
The beat must work with the sample muted.
Add a counter-melody that appears only once.
Use the same sample for the melody and the drums.
No sound may be untouched by distortion.
Print all effects. No live plugins at the end.
Use only one instance of each plugin in the whole project.
Finish in 60 minutes.
Finish in 15 minutes.
Spend at least 20 minutes on the drums alone.
Do not undo. Ever.
Do not save until it's done.
Work with the screen brightness at minimum.
Make the whole beat with your eyes closed for the first 10 minutes.
Use a sample slower than 70 BPM in a beat faster than 140.
Time-stretch a 2-second sample across 4 bars.
Use only the tail of the sample, never the attack.
Filter the sample so only the bass frequencies remain.
Filter the sample so only the highs remain.
Layer two samples from completely different decades.
The loop must be an odd number of bars.
Add a 2-bar break where only percussion plays.
The last 8 bars must be completely different from the first 8.
No more than 4 elements playing at any moment.
At least 12 elements must play at the climax.
Use a sound you have never used before.
Delete the first idea you have and use the second.
The beat must be usable as a loop with no audible seam.
Include a swung and a straight section in the same track.
Use hand claps recorded by you.
No sound may repeat more than 8 times in a row.
Use a pitch bend on at least one instrument.
Detune two copies of the same sound by 12 cents.
The whole beat must be built on a single held chord.
Use a bass line that moves every beat.
The bass must play only on the downbeat.
Use a sample that makes you uncomfortable.
Make the beat feel warm using only cold sounds.
Make it danceable without a four-on-the-floor kick.
No sound may be quantized to less than a quarter note.
Include a section with no low end at all.
High-pass everything except the kick at 200Hz.
Use only one reverb preset for the entire project.
Do not touch the master fader.
Keep the peak below -6dB the whole time.
Clip the master on purpose and make it sound good.
The intro and the outro must be the same 4 bars.
Write a 4-bar melody, then use only its inversion.
The drum pattern must change every 8 bars.
Use a triplet hat pattern in a straight beat.
Put the snare on beat 3 only.
Use two kicks with different tunings.
Add a ghost note pattern under the snare.
The hats must never land on a downbeat.
Use a shaker instead of hi-hats.
Use only one drum sample, pitched differently for each role.
Trigger a reverse cymbal before every section change.
Add a sound that only appears once in the whole track.
Every section must start with silence for one beat.
Use a wrong note on purpose and keep it.
Sample a sound from outside your window.
Sample a sound from a movie you've never seen.
Use vinyl noise as the only percussion in the intro.
The melody must be played on an instrument you can't play.
Record everything at half speed, then play it back at full.
Play the sample at double speed and build around it.
Use a loop that fights the drum pattern rhythmically.
The drums and the sample must be in different time feels.
No sound may have an attack faster than 20ms.
All sounds must be gated to a very short release.
The beat must have exactly two sections and nothing else.
Build the beat around a bass line with no chords.
Use a chord progression from a song you love, but change the rhythm.
Never use a sound at 100% volume.
Use a low-pass filter automation as the only transition tool.
The last chord must be a different quality than the first.
Use a sample of a crowd, applause, or laughter.
Include a moment where everything drops out except one sound.
Make the beat without ever soloing a channel.
Only use effects that were on the master when you started.
Use a synth you have never opened before.
Do not use the mouse for anything musical.
The project must contain no more than 3 audio files.
Everything must be exported and reimported at least once.
Use a sound from an instrument in your room.
The beat must have no melody, only texture and rhythm.
Build the drums last.
Make the loop 3 bars long instead of 4.
Use a swing setting above 60%.
Play the chords with your non-dominant hand only.
Do not listen to any reference track while working.
Pick a colour and make the beat sound like it.
Make it sound like it's playing in the next room.
Make it sound like a memory, not a recording.
Every sound must be affected by the same LFO.
Add wow and flutter to the entire mix.
The beat must survive being played on a phone speaker.
Use a sample and never repeat the same slice twice.
Write the drum pattern on paper before opening the DAW.
The track must end abruptly, mid-phrase.
Include a key change up a semitone at the end.
Do not add anything after the 30-minute mark. Only subtract.
Use only sounds that fit in one sampler instance.
The whole beat must be under 60 seconds.
Add a live element you performed, even badly.
Use a rhythm from a genre outside hip-hop.

extraChallenges.text: Only use one sample.
Do not use any synths.
Everything must be under 10 tracks.
Finish it in one sitting.
Post it publicly, whatever it sounds like.
Give it a title before you press play.
Make a second version at half the tempo.
Make a second version with no drums.
Send it to someone before you sleep.
Do not mix it. Raw levels only.
Add a skit at the start.
Include a sound from outside.
Loop it for 10 minutes and see if it still holds.
Rewrite the drums after you finish, from scratch.
Add a 4-bar intro that uses none of the beat's sounds.
Use no more than 3 plugins total.
Cut the arrangement in half when you're done.
Add a completely unrelated outro.
Make the beat switch at bar 32.
Write a hook melody you could sing.
Do not use presets for the drums.
Sample yourself talking.
Use the same loop for the whole track without filtering it.
Add vinyl noise and never remove it.
Do the whole thing on headphones at low volume.
No looking at reference tracks.
Bounce it and don't open the project again.
Name every track in the session properly.
Make an alternate version in a major key.
Make an alternate version in double time.
Add one sound that shouldn't be there.
Record the melody in one take, keep the mistakes.
Use no sample packs at all.
Use only sample packs. Nothing recorded or played.
Give the beat a visual: one image that matches it.
Write two bars of lyrics over it.
Make it 20% shorter than feels right.
Add an element that only enters in the last 8 bars.
Use the same sound for the bass and the lead.
Make the transition between sections with silence only.
Add a texture layer you can barely hear.
Only work on it standing up.
No coffee, no phone, until it's done.
Do not rename or move any file while working.
Export a stem set when you're finished.
Try to make it sound expensive with cheap tools.
Make the drums groove without any swing setting.
Include one sound played backwards and pitched down.
Add a second percussion layer that doubles the swing.
Make it work as an intro track for an album.
Make it work as the last track on an album.
Only use sounds from a single folder.
Change one thing every time you loop it.
Add a build-up with no drums in it.
Automate the pan of one element across the whole track.
Use no more than two colours in your session view.
Keep the CPU under 30%.
Do not use any third-party reverb.
The whole beat must fit in 16 bars.
Add a completely dry section with zero effects.
Make a lofi version and a clean version.
Use one sound source for every element.
Add a subtle detune to every melodic layer.
Give the beat one moment of surprise.
Do not use a limiter.
Make it sound old without using vinyl effects.
Make it sound modern using only vintage sources.
Sample a sound from a device in your house.
Include a rhythm played on a non-instrument.
Every element must enter one at a time in the intro.
Do not use the piano roll for the drums.
Try to finish before the coffee gets cold.
Add a section that would fit a completely different genre.
End with the same sound you started with.
Never look at the master meter.
Write the arrangement before making any sound.
Use only one bar of source material.
Make the bass and the kick share the same envelope.
Add a sound that pans across the stereo field once.
Give it a proper fade-in and fade-out.
Use no more than 12 notes total in the melody.
Mute the sample for 4 bars somewhere.
Make the drums the last thing you touch.
Use a random plugin preset and build from it.
Do not use any sound you used in your last beat.
Add a subtle noise layer that changes every 8 bars.
Make it loopable as a 15-second clip.
Use only two velocities across all drums.
Give one element a completely different reverb than everything else.
Record a room tone and put it under the whole track.
No copying a pattern more than 4 times.
Add a moment where the beat almost stops.
Make the hook out of a chopped word.
Use a sound from a phone notification.
Add tape hiss to the drums only.
Do not add anything in the last 10 minutes.
Make it good enough to send to an artist tonight.
Explain the beat in one sentence when you're done.
Play it once at full volume before deciding it's finished.
Keep the first idea, no matter what.
Make the beat in a DAW you rarely use.
Add one element from a genre you never touch.
No hi-hats at all.
Add a bar of pure noise as a transition.
Only use two octaves of the keyboard.
Make the melody out of a bass sound.
Give the track a 4-bar ambient tail.
Use a sample from a language you don't understand.
Keep everything below -3dB and never touch the limiter.
Make it feel like the middle of a longer song.
Do not use any drum fill.
Add one long note that lasts 8 bars.
Layer two drum breaks instead of one.
Only use sounds you can name from memory.
Give the beat a fake vinyl intro with needle drop.
Save the project with a name that describes the feeling.
Add nothing after the drums are done.
Make a version that works without the melody.
Use only one plugin chain, copied to every track.
Finish it even if you hate it.

mixNotes: Leave headroom. The loop should breathe.
Commit to the sound early. Print it.
Mix at low volume for the first 20 minutes.
Check it in mono before you finish.
If it works on one speaker, it works.
Do the arrangement before the mix, always.
Turn things down instead of turning things up.
Sit the drums under the sample, not on top of it.
The best EQ move is deleting the track.
